	<Item Name="title" Type="String">The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock</Item>
	<Item Name="summary" Type="String">Hundreds of bacterial small open reading frames (sORFs) encoding microproteins of fewer than fifty amino acids have recently been identified. Biological functions have been ascribed to an increasing number of microproteins, some of which play roles in bacterial stress responses. In this work, we provide evidence that GndA, a frameshifted 36-amino acid microprotein encoded in an internal open reading frame (intORF) overlapping the 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (6PGD) coding sequence, functions in the response to heat shock. We demonstrate independent contributions of GndA and 6PGD to cell growth at high temperature. GndA is highly hydrophobic and associates with pyruvate dehydrogenase and respiratory complex I. Consistent with a role in cellular homeostasis, GndA mutations alter the transcriptional responses to heat shock. These results suggest that GndA promotes bacterial cell growth at high temperature via a mechanism distinct from that of the 6PGD protein that it overlaps. GndA thus expands the paradigm of bacterial microproteins that function in cellular stress responses.</Item>

text:
Abstract
Objective: to enumerate every GEO Series entry reporting Escherichia coli heat‑shock expression data and provide their accessions. Approach: we queried NCBI GEO’s gds index via Entrez E-utilities with organism=“Escherichia coli” and heat‑shock terms (“heat shock”, “heat‑shock”, “heat stress”), restricted to Series records (gse[Entry Type]). We then resolved each matching UID to its accession and title using esummary. Results: the query returned 57 Series UIDs; all were resolved to GSE accessions and study titles. These include array- and sequencing-based expression profiling studies spanning K-12 MG1655 and pathogenic strains, time courses, stress combinations, and sigma 32/rpoH-related programs. Significance: this curated list consolidates heat‑shock transcriptomics resources for E. coli, enabling reuse in meta-analysis, benchmarking, and pipeline testing. Provenance: one esearch call (Count=57) and three esummary calls (chunked to avoid truncation) from NCBI E-utilities; URLs are provided for reproducibility.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli’s heat-shock response is a canonical bacterial stress program mediated primarily by sigma 32 (RpoH), encompassing chaperones, proteases, and proteostasis regulators. Gene-expression studies under heat shock reveal kinetics, magnitude, and strain-specific regulatory features crucial for systems biology, biotechnology, and stress-engineering.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. A single, current list of E. coli heat‑shock expression studies and their GEO accessions was not consolidated.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: list all E. coli heat‑shock expression studies in GEO Series with their GSE accessions. Hypothesis: an organism- and keyword-restricted Entrez search of GEO’s gds index will comprehensively capture the set of series records referencing heat shock/stress in E. coli.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted NCBI GEO’s gds index via Entrez E-utilities to obtain a count and identifiers for E. coli heat‑shock Series records. We then resolved each UID to its Series accession and metadata using esummary. The esummary step was chunked to avoid server-side truncation.

Materials.
- NCBI GEO (gds index), accessed via functions.ncbi_entrez_raw (esearch, esummary).

Procedures.
- Entrez esearch (gds):
  - utility='esearch'
  - db='gds'
  - term='Escherichia coli[ORGN] AND ("heat shock"[All Fields] OR "heat-shock"[All Fields] OR "heat stress"[All Fields]) AND gse[Entry Type]'
  - retmax=9999
- Entrez esummary (gds), chunked to prevent truncation:
  - Call 1:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'
    - id='200330026,200269907,200305556,200305476,200283264,200272161,200272160,200272159,200272158,200289056,200281945,200206340,200195509,200233555,200211825'
  - Call 2:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'
    - id='200223913,200064021,200153497,200216100,200200758,200189206,200173614,200144943,200144942,200060669,200060668,200060667,200151940,200137362,200103421'
  - Call 3:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'
    - id='200090056,200085807,200061749,200068762,200061738,200061736,200046740,200046737,200047509,200033212,200040557,200039439,200028320,200034590,200027607,200020305,200016973,200013698,200015588,200015534,200018362,200017507,200017074,200011463,200007656,200004511,200004321'

Statistical Analysis.
- Total series count (57) was taken from esearch ‘Count’.
- Series UIDs were taken from esearch ‘IdList’. Each UID was resolved to accession (Item Name="Accession") and title (Item Name="title") via esummary. No duplicates were present (57 distinct UIDs).
- Inclusion reflects the esearch term scope (E. coli AND heat-shock/-stress AND Series).

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1 lists all 57 E. coli heat‑shock Series studies with accessions and titles.

Table 1. E. coli heat-shock GEO Series (GSE accessions and titles)
- GSE330026 — The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock

summary.answer:
Abstract
Objective: to enumerate every GEO Series entry reporting Escherichia coli heat‑shock expression data and provide their accessions. Approach: we queried NCBI GEO’s gds index via Entrez E-utilities with organism=“Escherichia coli” and heat‑shock terms (“heat shock”, “heat‑shock”, “heat stress”), restricted to Series records (gse[Entry Type]). We then resolved each matching UID to its accession and title using esummary. Results: the query returned 57 Series UIDs; all were resolved to GSE accessions and study titles. These include array- and sequencing-based expression profiling studies spanning K-12 MG1655 and pathogenic strains, time courses, stress combinations, and sigma 32/rpoH-related programs. Significance: this curated list consolidates heat‑shock transcriptomics resources for E. coli, enabling reuse in meta-analysis, benchmarking, and pipeline testing. Provenance: one esearch call (Count=57) and three esummary calls (chunked to avoid truncation) from NCBI E-utilities; URLs are provided for reproducibility.

I. Introduction
Background. Escherichia coli’s heat-shock response is a canonical bacterial stress program mediated primarily by sigma 32 (RpoH), encompassing chaperones, proteases, and proteostasis regulators. Gene-expression studies under heat shock reveal kinetics, magnitude, and strain-specific regulatory features crucial for systems biology, biotechnology, and stress-engineering.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. A single, current list of E. coli heat‑shock expression studies and their GEO accessions was not consolidated.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: list all E. coli heat‑shock expression studies in GEO Series with their GSE accessions. Hypothesis: an organism- and keyword-restricted Entrez search of GEO’s gds index will comprehensively capture the set of series records referencing heat shock/stress in E. coli.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We targeted NCBI GEO’s gds index via Entrez E-utilities to obtain a count and identifiers for E. coli heat‑shock Series records. We then resolved each UID to its Series accession and metadata using esummary. The esummary step was chunked to avoid server-side truncation.

Materials.
- NCBI GEO (gds index), accessed via functions.ncbi_entrez_raw (esearch, esummary).

Procedures.
- Entrez esearch (gds):
  - utility='esearch'
  - db='gds'
  - term='Escherichia coli[ORGN] AND ("heat shock"[All Fields] OR "heat-shock"[All Fields] OR "heat stress"[All Fields]) AND gse[Entry Type]'
  - retmax=9999
- Entrez esummary (gds), chunked to prevent truncation:
  - Call 1:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'
    - id='200330026,200269907,200305556,200305476,200283264,200272161,200272160,200272159,200272158,200289056,200281945,200206340,200195509,200233555,200211825'
  - Call 2:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'

  - Call 3:
    - utility='esummary'
    - db='gds'
    - id='200090056,200085807,200061749,200068762,200061738,200061736,200046740,200046737,200047509,200033212,200040557,200039439,200028320,200034590,200027607,200020305,200016973,200013698,200015588,200015534,200018362,200017507,200017074,200011463,200007656,200004511,200004321'

Statistical Analysis.
- Total series count (57) was taken from esearch ‘Count’.
- Series UIDs were taken from esearch ‘IdList’. Each UID was resolved to accession (Item Name="Accession") and title (Item Name="title") via esummary. No duplicates were present (57 distinct UIDs).
- Inclusion reflects the esearch term scope (E. coli AND heat-shock/-stress AND Series).
